                                                           SPECIAL NOTICES
The geographical coordinates published in the Designated               Examples
Airspace Handbook (DAH) conform to formatting                          Hundredths of a Second
requirements of ICAO Annex 15 and Doc 8126:                                   The most stringent ICAO accuracy requires
 •   Latitude is given first, presented as DDMM[SS.s]H where                  some geographical coordinates to be given in
     DD denotes degrees; MM denotes minutes; SS denotes                       hundredths of a second. Thus, the delineation of
     seconds; s denotes tenths or hundredths of seconds; and                  five degrees, seven minutes and twenty-one
     H denotes hemisphere, N for North or S for South. Two                    point two-zero seconds South, sixty-five
     digits are used in expressing values of less than 10                     degrees, twenty-five minutes and twenty-two
     degrees of latitude;                                                     point six-two seconds East will be presented as:
                                                                              050721.20S 0652522.62E.
 •   Longitude is presented as DDDMM[SS.s]H where DDD
     denotes degrees; MM denotes minutes; SS denotes                   Tenth of a Second
     seconds; s denotes tenths or hundredths of seconds; and                   Should the above example be required to an
     H denotes hemisphere, W for West or E for East. Three                     accuracy of one tenth of a second, it will be
     digits are used in expressing values of less than 100                     presented as: 050721.2S 0652522.6E.
     degrees of longitude;                                             Seconds
 •   Symbols for degrees, minutes or seconds are omitted;                    Should the above example be required to an
                                                                             accuracy of one second, it will be presented as:
 •   The resolution used for geographical coordinates
                                                                             050721S 0652523E.
     conforms with the aeronautical data quality requirements
     listed in ICAO Annex 15 Appendix 7;                               Minutes
                                                                                 Should the above example be required to an
 •   Where a degree of accuracy of decimals of seconds is
                                                                                 accuracy of one minute (i.e. 1NM) it will be
     required, the number of decimal places is always
                                                                                 presented as: 0507S 06525E.
     consistent within the set;
 •   The points defining lateral limits of an irregular shape are
     listed in clockwise order separated by a hyphen “–”. The
     last point on the list is the same as the first point.
 •   A circular shape area is defined by the word “radius”
     followed by the value of the radius in nautical miles (NM),
     followed by the words “centre”, followed by coordinates of
     the centre of the circle.

                                 SECTION 13 – SPECIAL USE AIRSPACE
AIRSPACE NAME
Airspace is named according to the general commonly known geographic region, e.g. R237 WOOMERA.
Where a more specific name is required, that name will be placed after the regional name in brackets, e.g. R736 TOWNSVILLE (STAR),
where “Star” is the name of a property in that region.
SPECIAL USE AIRSPACE (SUA) CONTACT DETAILS
Refer ERSA for all SUA contact phone numbers.

RESTRICTED AREA (RA) STATUS LEGEND
Conditional RA Status
In order to assist with shared use of airspace, all restricted areas have been allocated an ‘RA Status’. This status will give an indication as to
the likelihood of obtaining a clearance to fly through restricted airspace. NOTAM may be issued to indicate changes to the RA Status; which
should be checked prior to flight planning.
Conditional RA1: Pilots may flight plan through the Restricted Area and under normal circumstances expect a clearance from ATC.
Conditional RA2: Pilots must not flight plan through the Restricted Area unless on a route specified in ERSA GEN FPR or under agreement
with the Controlling Authority, however a clearance from ATC is not assured. Other tracking may be offered through the Restricted Area on a
tactical basis.
Conditional RA3: Pilots must not flight plan through the Restricted Area and clearances will not be available.
MILITARY OPERATING AREAS
MOA are a subset of Danger Areas. They are primarily established outside Australian territory in Australian-administered airspace for use by
the Australian Defence Force for military training and exercises. Outside Australian territory, only Australian aircraft are restricted from entering
MOA unless they have Administering Authority approval. Within Australian territory, both foreign registered and Australian aircraft are restricted
from entering MOA unless they have Administering Authority approval. It is highly recommended that foreign registered aircraft make
appropriate safety contact with the relevant Administering Authority if they choose to enter an active MOA outside Australian territory.
